Source: Steps 1, 6 and 7 of the selected proof (the interior product ♭, the action identity S′ = A₁ + (A₂ + E′), and the mass chain), stated for currents A₁, A₂ given by their action formulas (in the selected node they come from two applications of the selected node's own product_current dependency) and for an arbitrary set W. One simplification: integrability of the S₀′-slices on Q_r is taken from part (iii) of slice_integrable (R₀′ is carried by G^⊥ by hypothesis) instead of part (ii). The selected proof is the project's argument for Simon, Lemma 7.3.5 (book/chapter-07.txt, lines 407–417), whose proof Simon leaves to the reader.
Inherited results cited by exact Lean name (dependencies of the parent node competitor_mass):
 (IP) Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_interior_product, part (a): for all k, m, n′, every g : Fin k → Euclid P and h : n′ = k + m there is a continuous linear ♭ : Λ^{n′} → Λ^m with ♭α v = α(Fin.append g v ∘ Fin.cast h).
 (SI) Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_slice_integrable, part (iii): if g is orthonormal, T ∈ 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) is represented by R_T with R_T.measure(ℝ^P ∖ (span g)^⊥) = 0, Φ : Λ^{n′} → Λ^j is continuous linear and ω is a test n′-form, then t ↦ currentEval T (y ↦ Φ(ω(t + y))) is μHE[k]-integrable on every Borel E ⊆ span g.
 (MT) Submission.lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq: if X, Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_k(U), |c| ≤ 1 and Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G, then M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
Notation. G := span g (as a set), Q_r := {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r ∀ i}, H^k := μHE[k], ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n).

1. (A continuous ♭.) By (IP)(a) with k, m, n, g, h there is a continuous linear ♭ : Λ^n → Λ^m with ♭α v = α(Fin.append g v ∘ Fin.cast h) for all α, v. Its underlying function satisfies the defining identity required in each of the four formula hypotheses, so they all hold with flat := ♭.
2. (Borel sets.) G is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). Q_r = G ∩ ⋂_i {t : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r} is closed (each set is closed by continuity of t ↦ |⟨g_i, t⟩|). So G and Q_r are Borel, and Q_r ⊆ G.
3. (currentEval of a difference.) For every m-form φ: currentEval (S₀′ − S₀) φ = currentEval S₀′ φ − currentEval S₀ φ. If φ is a test form with tsupport φ ⊆ ℝ^P, both sides equal S₀′(φ) − S₀(φ), because the contract difference is evaluated termwise; otherwise both sides are 0 = 0 − 0 by the definition of currentEval.
4. (Integrability.) Fix a test n-form ω and put f₀(t) := currentEval S₀ (y ↦ ♭(ω̂(t + y))) and f₀′(t) := currentEval S₀′ (y ↦ ♭(ω̂(t + y))). By (SI)(iii) with T := S₀, R_T := R₀ (μ₀ carried by G^⊥) and the Borel sets E := G, E := Q_r ⊆ G, f₀ is H^k-integrable on G and on Q_r. By (SI)(iii) with T := S₀′, R_T := R₀′ (μ₀′ carried by G^⊥) and E := Q_r, f₀′ is H^k-integrable on Q_r.
5. (The action identity.) By the hypotheses with flat := ♭ and by step 3:
 S′(ω) = S(ω) + Z(ω) = ∫_G f₀ dH^k + (∫_{Q_r} (f₀′ − f₀) dH^k + E′(ω)).
 By step 4, ∫_{Q_r}(f₀′ − f₀) = ∫_{Q_r} f₀′ − ∫_{Q_r} f₀ (integral_sub), and, as Q_r ⊆ G is Borel and f₀ is integrable on G, ∫_{G∖Q_r} f₀ = ∫_G f₀ − ∫_{Q_r} f₀ (setIntegral_sdiff). Hence
 S′(ω) = ∫_{G∖Q_r} f₀ dH^k + (∫_{Q_r} f₀′ dH^k + E′(ω)) = A₁(ω) + (A₂(ω) + E′(ω)),
 by the formulas for A₁ and A₂ with flat := ♭.
6. (The current T₂ = A₂ + E′.) Let T₂ := A₂ − (0 − E′) (contract difference and zero current). Then T₂(ω) = A₂(ω) − (0 − E′(ω)) = A₂(ω) + E′(ω) for every test n-form ω.
7. (Mass chain.) By (MT) with U := ℝ^P, G := W and c := 1 (|1| ≤ 1): from S′(ω) = A₁(ω) + 1·T₂(ω) for all ω (steps 5–6), M_W(S′) ≤ M_W(A₁) + M_W(T₂); from T₂(ω) = A₂(ω) + 1·E′(ω) for all ω, M_W(T₂) ≤ M_W(A₂) + M_W(E′). Finally M_W(E′) ≤ M_{ℝ^P}(E′) = M(E′) (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono with W ⊆ ℝ^P; the mass is the local mass on the whole domain ℝ^P).
8. (Conclusion.) Combining step 7 by monotonicity of addition in [0, ∞]: M_W(S′) ≤ M_W(A₁) + (M_W(A₂) + M(E′)) = M_W(A₁) + M_W(A₂) + M(E′). ∎
